title: EV Charger Rebates in Squamish 2026: Up to $500 With the Local Top-Up
desc: Squamish homeowners get 75% of a Level 2 charger's cost back, up to $500: BC Hydro's $350 plus the District of Squamish's $150 top-up. Plus $200 for a power management device.
badge: Up to $500 with the local top-up
lead: Squamish is one of the few places in BC where the local government adds to BC Hydro's home charger rebate. Together you can get back 75% of the cost of a Level 2 charger, up to $500.
cards_heading: What EV charger rebates pay in Squamish
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's home charger and local top-up pages on October 3, 2026.

cards.title: BC Hydro charger rebate
cards.note: 50% of the cost of buying and installing a Level 2 charger.

cards.title: District of Squamish top-up
cards.note: Added on automatically. Brings the total to 75%, up to $500.

cards.title: Power management device
cards.note: Can help you avoid an electrical panel upgrade.

cards.title: Peak Saver smart charger
cards.note: Bill credit for enrolling an eligible smart charger.

after_cards:
A Squamish example

A charger and install cost $1,000. BC Hydro pays 50%, capped at $350. The District of Squamish top-up adds $150, for $500 back. Add a power management device and get $200 more, as long as total incentives stay under what you paid.
sections: The District of Squamish adds up to $150 to BC Hydro's charger rebate. Together they cover 75% of the cost, up to $500. There is no extra form: BC Hydro adds it when it approves your rebate, as long as your address is in the district.

Squamish's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 0.2°C, but the coldest reading was -28.1°C. On the coldest days a car loses range and charges more slowly, so a garage or a car that preheats while plugged in helps. Squamish's housing is fairly new: only 1,645 of 9,185 households own a detached house built before 1981. Newer homes are more likely to have panel room for a charger, but ask the electrician to check before you buy a power management device.

Squamish has 9,185 households and about 70% own. Row homes and duplexes qualify for the home charger rebate just like detached houses, so a townhome owner with their own parking spot can apply. In a strata, get written approval to run power to your stall first. If the building wants chargers for many owners, the District's multi-unit EV Ready top-up is the better route.

A Level 2 charger runs on 240 volts and can fill most cars overnight. Choose one on BC Hydro's eligible list. If you want the Peak Saver credit too, pick a smart charger that BC Hydro lists for Peak Saver. During a few winter peak events, November to March, BC Hydro may slow your charging for up to four hours; you can opt out of events.
Who in Squamish can use it

The rebate is for single-family homes, row homes and duplexes. The 2021 Census counted 9,185 households in Squamish; 41% (3,730) live in a detached house and about 70% own. If you live in an apartment or condo, BC Hydro has separate multi-unit building rebates, and the District of Squamish also offers multi-unit top-ups of up to $1,000 for EV Ready plans and charger installs.

Many older homes do not have spare room in the electrical panel for a 40 or 50 amp charger. A power management device shares power between the charger and the rest of the house, so you may skip a costly panel upgrade. BC Hydro adds $200 for one. All incentives together cannot be more than what you paid.
Tesla chargers are not eligible for BC Hydro or CleanBC rebates. Pick a charger from BC Hydro's eligible list.
Send proof of purchase and installation within six months (180 days) of the install. Keep the electrical permit and the itemized invoice.
claim_steps: Pick an eligible Level 2 charger (not Tesla).
Have a licensed electrician install it, with a permit.
Apply to BC Hydro within 180 days with the invoice and proof of install.
BC Hydro adds the District of Squamish top-up on approval.
Enroll the charger in Peak Saver if it is eligible.
faq: Do I apply separately for the top-up?
No. BC Hydro adds the District of Squamish top-up when it approves your rebate.
Is a Tesla Wall Connector eligible?
No. Tesla chargers are not eligible.
What is the most I can get?
Up to $500 for the charger with the top-up, $200 for a power management device, and a $250 Peak Saver credit, capped at what you paid.
Not this rebate. BC Hydro has separate rebates for multi-unit buildings.
I live just outside Squamish. Do I get the top-up?
The top-up is for addresses inside the District of Squamish. Outside it, you still get BC Hydro's rebate of up to $350.
Do I need an electrical permit?
Ask your electrician. A permit and an itemized invoice make the claim easier to prove.
